t: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall be available from November 20, 1979, and shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) September 30, 1980, whichever first occurs.

fable.w: This section only sets the period during which continuing-resolution appropriations remain available. The one tempting element is the reference to action by both Houses, but Congress is inside the federal government and enacting legislation is not consultation with outside parties. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with non-federal actors, or right to sue.
fable.s: enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity

qwen_chat.w: This section solely defines the time period during which appropriated funds are available for use. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The actors mentioned are Congress and the executive branch (via the appropriation acts), which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall be available from November 20, 1979, and shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) September 30, 1980, whichever first occurs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for projects, there is an implicit process involving outside parties. However, the text itself only defines the temporal availability of funds and does not mention any consultation, hearing, or interaction with non-federal entities.
